title: 2001 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 3
statement: There are some red and blue marbles in a box. We are told that there are twelve more red marbles than blue marbles, and we experimentally determine that when we pick a marble randomly we get a blue marble one quarter of the time. How many marbles are there in the box?

solutions.text: Call the number of blue marbles \(x\), so the number of red marbles is \(x+12\) and the total number of marbles is \(2 x+12\). The probability of picking a red marble is \(\frac{x}{2 x+12}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow x=6\), so \(2 x+12=24\).
